<h2 class="nv-section-title"><a href="/docs/rules/tooling/what-the-toolchain-is/">What the toolchain is</a><span class="nv-section-count">4</span></h2>
<p class="nv-section-blurb">No REPL, reflection and parsing built in, and the two claims the project will not make against Python.</p>
<ol class="nv-rule-list"><li><a href="/docs/rules/tooling/what-the-toolchain-is/#shebang-opens-code-mode">A file whose first two bytes are <code>#!</code> starts in code mode, and its first line is trivia</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/tooling/what-the-toolchain-is/#no-repl">There is no REPL and none is planned; <code>nvs run</code>, <code>nvs test</code> and <code>Core\Debug::dump</code> are the answer</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/tooling/what-the-toolchain-is/#reflection-and-source-parsing-are-core-features">Reflection and source parsing are built into <code>Core</code>, and <code>Core\Ast</code> is the compiler's own parser</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/tooling/what-the-toolchain-is/#python-claims">Against Python, Novis claims the tool that gets handed over; &quot;faster than Python&quot; and &quot;replaces Python&quot; are forbidden</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span></li></ol>
</section>

<section class="nv-section">
<h2 class="nv-section-title"><a href="/docs/rules/tooling/the-formatter/">The formatter</a><span class="nv-section-count">13</span></h2>
<p class="nv-section-blurb">One canonical style, no configuration, no reflowing of what you wrote — and a fixed point over the input bytes.</p>
<ol class="nv-rule-list"><li><a href="/docs/rules/tooling/the-formatter/#fmt-is-one-canonical-style"><code>nvs fmt</code> has one style, takes no configuration, and its output is a pure function of the file it is given</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/tooling/the-formatter/#fmt-base-style-is-per">The base style is PER: four-space indentation, K&amp;R braces on control structures, Allman braces on declarations, and one canonical modifier order</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/tooling/the-formatter/#fmt-never-reflows"><code>nvs fmt</code> never decides where an expression breaks: the author's own line breaks are kept and only what surrounds them is normalized</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/tooling/the-formatter/#fmt-quotes">A string literal is rewritten to single quotes unless it interpolates or contains a single quote, and heredoc bodies and comments are never touched</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/tooling/the-formatter/#fmt-trailing-commas">A comma-separated list that spans more than one line gets a trailing comma, and a list on one line never does</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/tooling/the-formatter/#fmt-sorts-the-use-block">Consecutive <code>use</code> declarations are sorted by full path, ascending and case-sensitive, with no blank line between them</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/tooling/the-formatter/#fmt-novis-constructs">Every construct PER never saw — qualifiers, <code>lateinit</code>, <code>fn</code> closures, <code>match</code>, object literals, shape types, enum cases, markup literals, a <code>?&gt;</code> on its own line — has exactly one layout</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/tooling/the-formatter/#fmt-normalizes-only-reserved-spellings"><code>nvs fmt</code> lower-cases a mis-cased reserved spelling only where that spelling has no other legal meaning — a duration unit and the open tag, never a keyword or an identifier</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/tooling/the-formatter/#fmt-never-inserts-visibility"><code>nvs fmt</code> never inserts a visibility keyword; <code>nvs convert</code> inserts <code>public</code> as an E-tier rewrite</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/tooling/the-formatter/#fmt-never-reorders-members"><code>nvs fmt</code> never reorders class members, because declaration order is observable in what a program prints and sends</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/tooling/the-formatter/#fmt-is-idempotent"><code>nvs fmt</code> is a fixed point over the input bytes: byte-stable on every machine, and deliberately not source-independent</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/tooling/the-formatter/#fmt-is-never-a-diagnostic"><code>nvs fmt</code> is a separate opt-in tool: no compiler command runs it, an unformatted file is never a diagnostic, and an editor composes it with quick fixes in the client</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/tooling/the-formatter/#fmt-check-writes-nothing"><code>nvs fmt</code> rewrites in place; <code>--check</code> writes nothing and exits non-zero naming every file that would change; <code>--diff</code> prints the diff instead</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li></ol>
</section>
<section class="nv-section">
<h2 class="nv-section-title"><a href="/docs/rules/tooling/doc-comments-and-metadata/">Doc comments and <code>nvs meta</code></a><span class="nv-section-count">14</span></h2>
<p class="nv-section-blurb">A doc comment is exactly <code>///</code>, and one JSON document is the machine-readable source every renderer consumes.</p>
<ol class="nv-rule-list"><li><a href="/docs/rules/tooling/doc-comments-and-metadata/#doc-comment-is-three-slashes">A doc comment is exactly <code>///</code>; <code>////</code> and longer runs are ordinary comments, and <code>#</code> never is one</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="designed">Designed</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/tooling/doc-comments-and-metadata/#doc-comment-attaches-to-the-next-declaration">A <code>///</code> run attaches to the declaration below it across no blank line, and a doc comment attached to nothing is a diagnostic</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="designed">Designed</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/tooling/doc-comments-and-metadata/#doc-comment-tags-are-see-and-example">A doc comment is Markdown plus <code>@see</code> and <code>@example</code>, each of which must resolve, and any other <code>@tag</code> is a diagnostic</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="designed">Designed</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/tooling/doc-comments-and-metadata/#strict-docs">Nothing requires a doc comment by default; <code>nvs check --strict-docs</code> reports a public member without one, and no autofix can satisfy it</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="designed">Designed</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/tooling/doc-comments-and-metadata/#nvs-doc-renders-and-decides-nothing"><code>nvs doc &lt;entry&gt;</code> writes one Markdown page per class from the JSON and has no source of truth of its own</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/tooling/doc-comments-and-metadata/#one-json-several-renderers"><code>nvs meta --json</code> is the one machine-readable source of documentation, every renderer consumes it, and no renderer is authoritative for content</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="designed">Designed</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/tooling/doc-comments-and-metadata/#meta-json"><code>nvs meta --json</code> prints the whole <code>Core</code> registry as one JSON document, and a field with nothing written is an absent key rather than an empty one</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/tooling/doc-comments-and-metadata/#meta-json-takes-a-program"><code>nvs meta --json &lt;entry&gt;</code> emits that program's own declarations beside the <code>Core</code> registry, in the registry's own shape</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/tooling/doc-comments-and-metadata/#an-agent-asks-the-binary"><code>nvs agent</code> answers a coding agent from the registry and the embedded reference chapters in four commands, and the check loop is part of the surface</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/tooling/doc-comments-and-metadata/#the-index-is-one-line-per-member"><code>nvs agent index</code> prints one derived line per registered member, carrying its signature and the capability it is gated on, and one per chapter heading</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/tooling/doc-comments-and-metadata/#the-index-names-every-key-command-and-code"><code>nvs agent index</code> carries one derived line per configuration key, command, flag and diagnostic code, and <code>find</code> reaches each by the name a user types</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/tooling/doc-comments-and-metadata/#a-diagnostic-code-carries-its-card">Every diagnostic code carries a plain card that <code>nvs agent show</code> prints, and a terminal rendering names that command once</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="designed">Designed</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/tooling/doc-comments-and-metadata/#a-primer-claim-is-executed">The primer is generated, and every refusal it states and every example it shows is proven against the compiler that ships with it</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/tooling/doc-comments-and-metadata/#an-adapter-carries-protocol-and-never-language"><code>nvs agent init</code> writes one pointer per harness, and no adapter ever states a language fact</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="designed">Designed</span></li></ol>
</section>
<section class="nv-section">
<h2 class="nv-section-title"><a href="/docs/rules/tooling/nvs-convert/">Converting PHP</a><span class="nv-section-count">8</span></h2>
<p class="nv-section-blurb">One rule table read through two modes, every branch carrying a tier, and not one input byte dropped on the floor.</p>
<ol class="nv-rule-list"><li><a href="/docs/rules/tooling/nvs-convert/#convert-php-front-end">The PHP front end is <code>php-rs-parser</code>, pinned, reached only through <code>nvs_convert::php</code>, and never linked into the server</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="designed">Designed</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/tooling/nvs-convert/#convert-one-table-two-modes"><code>nvs convert</code> is one rule table read through two modes, and every branch carries a tier</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="designed">Designed</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/tooling/nvs-convert/#convert-three-tables">Names, constructs and semantic deltas each have one home, and the converter copies none of them</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="designed">Designed</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/tooling/nvs-convert/#convert-equivalent-is-proven">A tier-E rewrite names a differential case against the PHP oracle, or it is not E</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="designed">Designed</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/tooling/nvs-convert/#convert-is-deterministic"><code>nvs convert</code> is a pure function of its input bytes, mode, dialect, table digest and flags</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="designed">Designed</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/tooling/nvs-convert/#convert-drops-nothing">Every non-trivia input byte leaves the converter as code or as comment, and output is re-parsed before it is written</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="designed">Designed</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/tooling/nvs-convert/#convert-annotations-and-report">A converted site is annotated <code>TODO(convert:&lt;id&gt;)</code>, and <code>--check</code> publishes the tier counts as TOML</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="designed">Designed</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/tooling/nvs-convert/#convert-never-does">The converter never runs its input, never converts <code>vendor/</code> by default, never invents a binding and never claims compatibility</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="designed">Designed</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li></ol>
</section>
<section class="nv-section">
<h2 class="nv-section-title"><a href="/docs/rules/tooling/benchmarks-and-telemetry/">Benchmarks, telemetry and the update check</a><span class="nv-section-count">7</span></h2>
<p class="nv-section-blurb">Two independent opt-ins, both off by default, a closed set of counters, and a process serving traffic that never uploads.</p>
<ol class="nv-rule-list"><li><a href="/docs/rules/tooling/benchmarks-and-telemetry/#bench-engine-list-is-data">The benchmark engine list is data, <code>total</code> is the CLI headline, and a missing engine never turns a build red</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/tooling/benchmarks-and-telemetry/#telemetry-is-two-opt-ins">Usage telemetry and the update check are two independent opt-ins, both off by default, and neither ever implies the other</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="designed">Designed</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/tooling/benchmarks-and-telemetry/#telemetry-counters-are-a-closed-set">A counter is <code>invocation.&lt;subcommand&gt;</code> from the compiled-in command table or <code>invocation.unknown</code>, and nothing derived from traffic is ever counted</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="designed">Designed</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/tooling/benchmarks-and-telemetry/#telemetry-show-prints-the-payload"><code>nvs telemetry show</code> prints the exact payload the next upload would send, and the schema, the endpoint contracts and the aggregated data are all published</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="designed">Designed</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/tooling/benchmarks-and-telemetry/#a-serving-process-never-uploads">An upload carries only the previous finished week, rides a short-lived user-initiated command at most weekly, and a process that has bound a socket never uploads</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="designed">Designed</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/tooling/benchmarks-and-telemetry/#a-failed-upload-never-fails-the-command">An upload gets three seconds, is abandoned with its counters kept when that expires, says so, and never changes the carrying command's exit status</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="designed">Designed</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/tooling/benchmarks-and-telemetry/#update-check-states-the-whole-picture"><code>nvs update-check</code> always reports the telemetry switch, the local and latest versions, and with telemetry on its upload history; <code>--json</code> is stable and the exit status is always 0</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="designed">Designed</span></li></ol>
</section>
<section class="nv-section">
<h2 class="nv-section-title"><a href="/docs/rules/tooling/the-repository-tools/">The repository's own tools</a><span class="nv-section-count">5</span></h2>
<p class="nv-section-blurb">One Bun program, one JSON record per fact under <code>data/</code>, and generated files that are committed and never edited.</p>
<ol class="nv-rule-list"><li><a href="/docs/rules/tooling/the-repository-tools/#the-repository-tools-are-one-bun-program">The repository's tools are one Bun + TypeScript program, <code>bun nv</code>, and <code>smol-toml</code> is its only runtime dependency</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/tooling/the-repository-tools/#a-repository-fact-is-one-json-record">A fact a repository tool reads is one JSON record under <code>data/</code>, its type declared once and its text written by one writer</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/tooling/the-repository-tools/#a-rendered-file-is-committed-and-never-edited">A file rendered from the records is committed, marked generated and never edited, and a conflict in one is resolved by rendering it again</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/tooling/the-repository-tools/#the-chain-names-its-live-goal">The chain record names the live goal, and a goal's floor is a view over every walked goal's checks, with the permanent suite's tests graduated</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/tooling/the-repository-tools/#a-check-runs-only-when-the-change-reaches-its-footprint">A check runs only when the change reaches what its green runs were observed to use, and the pipeline runs and records on the one <code>covws</code> debug build</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span></li></ol>
</section>
</div>
